steps.visual_purpose: Show the class object Order separately from two instance objects, with first and second pointing to different instances and alias pointing to the same instance as first.

Make report.txt contents visible before and after each mode choice: reading preserves First, appending adds Second, write mode removes prior contents, and exclusive creation preserves an existing destination while raising FileExistsError.
Make the flow from Order("notebook", 3) through the initializer parameters to self.label and self.quantity visible, alongside the resulting notebook 3 output.
Show Order.add beside the call order.add(2), annotate order as the implicit self argument and 2 as amount, and make the change in order.quantity from 3 to 5 visible.

Make the implicit argument differences visible: an instance method receives self, Order.from_text receives cls and returns cls(int(text)), and Order.cost receives only its explicit quantity and price arguments.
Make the running example's delegation chain visible: report holds a Calculator object in self.calculator, Report.total(3) calls self.calculator.cost(3), and the collaborator returns 12.

Show annotated Order code distinguishing the public add method from the supporting self._quantity attribute, with the caller using order.add(2). Mark the underscore as a naming convention rather than an access restriction.
Show Order and FeeOrder together, highlighting the initialization sequence and the cost() call sequence: derived method, inherited calculation of 12, then addition of fee to produce 14.

Make the Exception subclass, the validator's raise statement, and the caller's matching handler visible together, with the negative-quantity control path marked from the validator to the recovery boundary.

Show the Order code and resulting labels values before and after the repair: initially both instances share one list; afterward each initialization creates a separate list, so changing first.labels leaves second.labels empty.
Make the transition from the Python record to JSON text and back to Python values visible, highlighting that the tuple nested within quantities returns as a list while active remains True.

Make the Order inspection expressions and their corresponding results visible together, highlighting quantity in the discovered names and distinguishing underscore-prefixed names as conventionally internal.

Show the explicit source and output paths before the operation, the constructed target = directory / filename, and the resulting directory contents after the report moves. Make the disappearance of the original source entry and appearance of the destination visible.
Make the Order methods and their resulting strings visible together, linking repr(order) to __repr__, str(order) and print(order) to __str__, and showing the fallback after __str__ is removed.
Make the explicit encoding argument visible in both text-file open calls, alongside the value café read from label.txt and preserved when written back.

Make the import boundary's three specific exception handlers and separate row-validation checks visible, with annotated DictReader results showing a missing quantity mapped to None and excess fields stored under the None key.

Show successful file entry followed by the indented body, with separate normal-completion and raised-exception paths both reaching file closure. Distinguish this file behavior from a general context manager's possible exception suppression.

Make the nested managed blocks, rb and wb modes, and unchanged bytes flowing from source.read() through payload to destination.write() visible; mark when each file closes and warn that opening copy.bin in wb replaces existing content.
